title: Give an infant CPR manikin two breaths with a bag-valve mask: mask sealed over nose and mouth, chest rising each time
instruction: Give the infant manikin two rescue breaths with the bag-valve mask: keep its head in the sniffing position, hold the mask sealed over its nose and mouth, squeeze the bag just until the chest rises each time, then lift the mask off its face and keep holding it.
context: Infant CPR is compressions and breaths, as "most cardiac arrests in infants and children have a respiratory etiology" (ILCOR 2025); the same bag-mask breaths serve the 6 million newborns a year who need basic resuscitation, "including bag-and-mask ventilation" (Wall 2009). The AHA BLS course tests two bag-mask breaths on an infant manikin, each over 1 second, with "visible chest rise with each breath". A robot giving them frees a lone rescuer for compressions. Here a real infant bag-valve mask meets a real infant CPR manikin whose airway closes if the head is flexed or over-extended. The 55 mm mask must land with its rim on the bridge of the nose and the chin, clear of the eyes, pressed on evenly without tipping the head. The bag sticks out 12 cm from the mask's centre, so the other hand must squeeze it about 25 mm without pushing it up or down: a push there tips the mask, its cuff lifts and the breath leaks. Squeezing much deeper over-inflates. No chest rise, no breath.
setup:
Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top.
- Mat. A 700 x 500 x 3 rubber non-slip mat, taped down, centred at x 500, y 0.
- Manikin. A Laerdal Little Baby QCPR infant CPR manikin (133-01050, light skin; 650 long, 260 wide, 1.8 kg; soft plastic skin over a plastic body; maker: "designed to represent a three-month-old infant"), its airway and lungs fitted as the maker shows and its QCPR feedback paired over Bluetooth with the Laerdal QCPR Learner app on a phone. It lies face up on the mat, centred on y 0, head toward the robot: crown at x 180, heels at x 830. The head rests on the back of the skull in its neutral position, eyes looking straight up, and tilts on its neck; maker: "Airway closes when neck is hyperextended or underextended". Bridge of the nose at x 260, 136 up; point of the chin at x 317, 131 up; eyes centred at x 260, y ±20.
- Chest flag. A stiff white card flag, 30 tall and 20 wide, taped upright with removable tape on the middle of the chest at the nipple line, x 400, y 0, its face toward +y, with a 10 mm black dot centred 20 above the skin. A phone on a tripod beside the table at x 400, y 700, level with the dot, films the flag face-on and the manikin's left side.
- Bag-valve mask. An Ambu SPUR II Infant (a thin-walled, frosted, slightly translucent bag 190 long, 71 across, 70 g; 40 cmH2O pressure-limiting valve; Ambu datasheet), its oxygen reservoir taken off, with its Ambu infant face mask (anatomical, clear PVC dome, PVC air-filled cuff; 55 long, 47 wide, 25 tall; 14 g) on the patient valve's swivel. It stands mask rim down on the mat at the manikin's left, mask centre at x 300, y 190, the mask's narrow (nose) end toward the robot. The bag points toward the robot along y 190, its far end resting on the table at x 80.
- The manikin's outline and the mask's start spot are marked on the mat with tape. Nothing else is on the table.
- Estimates: the face positions, the skin material, the bag's material (silicone) and the 6 kg infant the manikin stands for; the mask's sizes; the whole bag-valve mask's 110 g.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz), about 2.9 times the 833-step scripted demo
reset_notes: Lift the bag-valve mask off, let the bag refill, and stand it back on its tape mark, mask rim down, bag toward the robot. Return the manikin's head to neutral, eyes straight up, and the manikin to its tape outline; check the flag is upright on its tape and start a new session in the QCPR Learner app. Wipe the mask's cuff and the face with an alcohol wipe and let them dry. About 1 minute. The airway is replaced after each day's trials, as Laerdal advises after every class.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. Manikin: CC0 MakeHuman baby at the Little Baby's size, sculpted rigid face, loose on the mat; head hinged on the occiput, air passing only from 5° flexed to 15° back. Mask: anatomical dome, cuff as 12 sprung segments that follow the face. Bag: on the valve swivel, 4 sprung walls. No air: bvm_rules.py turns squeeze to volume (29.5 mL at 25 mm), passed only with all 12 segments in 1 mm; leak all-or-nothing; chest rises 0.25 mm/mL. Estimates: these numbers. Demo reads poses.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (after 1,040 of 2,400 steps the Dream API refused its next request: "DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction in this scene, refused: The instruction acts on a baby-like figure."; the scorer on its 1,040 actions gives 0); demo: 1.0
